issue.title: The global 'sase' on PATH is a uv tool install pinned to a separate checkout, so ad hoc 'sase init memory --check' compares a workspace against the wrong templates
issue.description:
ROOT CAUSE (verified in this environment, not inferred): /home/bryan/.local/bin/sase is a uv tool install -- its shebang is /home/bryan/.local/share/uv/tools/sase/bin/python3 -- editable-installed against a separate checkout at ~/projects/github/sase-org/sase. It is versioned independently of any ephemeral sase_<N> workspace. Proof at the time of filing: the global 'sase --help' prints a flat comma-separated subcommand list with no 'flag' entry, while this workspace's own .venv/bin/sase prints the current grouped help and 'sase flag --help' resolves to 'Inspect the code-owned SASE feature-flag registry and scaffold a new flag plus its dedicated removal bead'. Two different builds, both answering to the name 'sase'.

WHY IT MATTERS: memory-drift checking compares a checkout's COMMITTED memory files against the templates and generator carried by whichever sase build runs the check. just check's validate recipe pins {{venv_bin}}/sase, so it always matches the workspace tree and is trustworthy. But an agent that types a bare 'sase init memory --check' or 'sase memory init --check' -- exactly what the mandatory memory-init workflow invites -- runs the global build instead, comparing this workspace's committed files against a different checkout's templates. Whenever the two checkouts sit at different commits, that reports drift that does not exist in the tree under test (or hides drift that does).

WHY THIS IS PROBABLY THE ANSWER TO A LONG-RUNNING PUZZLE: task sase-n0 collected five independent reproductions across six agent shells between 2026-08-09 and 2026-08-17 of 'sase validate says green but sase init memory --check says drift', and sase-i7 was closed as superseded into it. Epic sase-ns.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.2 then established structurally that no generator divergence exists in source: sase validate's memory step shells out to '<sys.executable> -m sase init memory --check' as a subprocess, so both entry points funnel through the identical chain plan_init_memory -> _memory_root_plans -> plan_memory_root -> memory_root_context -> render_expected_memory_files()/provider_shim_plan(). Two entry points over one generator cannot disagree -- unless they are two different INSTALLS of that generator, which is precisely what a bare 'sase' versus '{{venv_bin}}/sase' gives you. The reported disagreements also match this shape: they were heading-style and memory-README-listing diffs, i.e. template-version skew rather than logic errors.

DECIDE AND IMPLEMENT ONE OF: (a) keep the global tool install synced with master -- a chezmoi apply hook, a post-merge reinstall, or a staleness warning the CLI prints when its own build predates the workspace it is invoked in; or (b) document that bare 'sase' memory-drift checks are unreliable outside just check, and make the mandatory memory-init workflow name the venv-pinned invocation explicitly wherever it appears in agent instructions. Option (a) is the durable fix; option (b) is cheap and immediate. They are not exclusive.

NOTE ON SCOPE: option (a) may reach the chezmoi repo, which must be opened through /sase_repo rather than by path. Editing generated memory files or agent instruction shims to carry option (b)'s wording requires explicit user permission per CLAUDE.md -- leave a TASK NEEDS APPROVAL note rather than editing them unilaterally.

PROPOSED BY: phase bead sase-ns.6.6.2 of epic sase-ns.6.6, as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note on 2026-08-17T08:20:46Z; routed to a task bead by that epic's land agent, which independently re-verified both installs.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-n0 — the task whose reported symptom this most likely explains ('sase validate and sase init memory --check disagree about sase/memory/sase_sizes.md'). Closed as done by epic sase-ns.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.2, which proved no generator divergence exists in source and landed the regression gate tests/main/test_init_memory_committed_drift.py. This task covers the remaining install-level mechanism, which that structural finding does not address.

RELATED: sase-i7 — closed as superseded by sase-n0 during the 2026-08-17 triage after collecting five independent reproductions of the same drift across six agent shells. Its evidence is the strongest corroboration that the disagreement is real and recurring even though the generator is single-sourced.
